In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ALOXE3-related ARCI is very rare, but not absent in East Asia.
ARCI caused by ALOXE3 has a wide geographic distribution and a wide range of phenotypes.
ALOXE3 gene mutations cause ARCI in East Asian patients as well as European patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a previously unreported ALOXE3 homozygous mutation in a consanguneous family from Japan.
the ALOXE3 gene is not only a candidate gene for LI in Europe, North Africa and the Middle East, South Asia, but also in East Asia.
ALOXE3 gene is a causative factor of ARCI, but the phenotype of ARCI caused by ALOXE3 can vary widely.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ALOXE3 gene analysis is useful for diagnosing ARCI in East Asia, where the frequency of ALOXE3 homozygous mutations is higher than in other regions.
ALOXE3-related ARCI can be found not only in Europe but also in East Asia, and that the ALOXE3 gene is an important ARCI gene in East Asia.
ALOXE3 gene analysis should be considered for ARCI cases with a severe phenotype, even in East Asian patients.
